analysis.one_liner: Shriram Finance is India's largest retail NBFC, lending against used commercial vehicles, two-wheelers, gold and small business/personal needs to borrowers banks often skip.
analysis.whats_happening: The stock has fallen about 24% from its August 6, 2026 peak of Rs 1,141 to Rs 865, after management cut FY27 AUM growth guidance to 15-17% from 18%, citing weak monsoon and drought conditions hitting demand in Maharashtra, Karnataka and Telangana, and analysts (Jefferies) warning credit costs could stay elevated for another one to two quarters. The August peak itself followed euphoria around Japan's MUFG Bank completing a Rs 39,618 crore (~$4.4 billion) investment for a 20% stake, announced in April 2026. The company also had to publicly deny an October 14, 2026 report suggesting MUFG was exploring raising its stake above 50%, calling it speculative. Next quarterly results are expected around late January 2027.
analysis.plain_terms: This is a lending business, not a bank - it borrows money and re-lends it to truck owners, bike buyers and small businesses, earning the gap between the two rates. A huge Japanese bank just bought a fifth of the company and loaded it with fresh capital, which is a strong vote of confidence and sharply lowers the risk of the balance sheet running short of capital. But right after that vote of confidence, management itself trimmed next year's growth target and flagged that bad-loan costs will stay higher for a bit longer - that is the tension: more capital cushion, slower near-term growth.
analysis.quarters: In the most recently reported quarter, net interest income was Rs 6,027 crore (+11.8% YoY), AUM grew to Rs 2.81 lakh crore (+15.7% YoY), but net interest margin slipped to 8.19% from 8.74% a year earlier. Gross Stage 3 (bad-loan equivalent) improved to 4.57% from 5.32%, and the credit cost ratio eased to 1.68%, though management guided to roughly 2% for the full year. Cost-to-income was 27.76%. Note: profit after tax is reported slightly differently across sources (around Rs 2,307 crore standalone versus Rs 2,314 crore consolidated) - this has not been reconciled here; check the company's exchange filing directly for the exact figure.
analysis.performance_read: Shareholder returns have been strong and have beaten the market by a wide margin: +23% over 1 year versus Nifty's -12.7%, +150% over 3 years versus Nifty's +18%, and +211% over 5 years versus Nifty's +25%. The company underwent a 1:5 stock split in January 2025 (already reflected in these return figures) and its listed history traces back through a 2022 three-way merger of Shriram Transport Finance, Shriram City Union Finance and Shriram Capital into the current entity - so returns before late 2022 technically belong to the predecessor Shriram Transport Finance stock, not a like-for-like continuation. The recent 24% drawdown from the August 2026 peak is a genuine price move tied to the guidance cut, not a corporate-action artifact - though the peak itself was inflated by one-time deal euphoria around the MUFG stake sale.
analysis.valuation_read: At roughly 21x earnings and 3.3x book value, the stock is not cheap by its own history or by typical NBFC standards. Some of that premium is earned - capital adequacy jumped to around 33-34% after the MUFG capital infusion, and CRISIL, ICRA and India Ratings all upgraded the company to AAA in 2026, which lowers its cost of borrowing over time. But the same equity issuance to MUFG diluted return on equity to about 12.76%, down from a historical mid-teens level, so investors are paying a higher multiple for a currently lower return on equity, betting that margins and growth recover.
analysis.growth_read: Growth so far has been volume-led: AUM is up nearly 16% year-on-year, while net interest margin has actually compressed (8.19% versus 8.74%), meaning the company is not relying on pricing power to grow. That is a healthier mix than margin-led growth in a lending business, but the guidance cut to 15-17% for FY27 suggests even volume growth is decelerating as rural demand softens.
analysis.health_read: Profits are backed by real collections rather than accounting adjustments - credit costs (1.68% this quarter, guided to ~2% for the year) and improving Stage 3 ratios (4.57%, down from 5.32%) suggest asset quality is stabilizing, not deteriorating sharply. Cost of borrowing (around 8.56% on average liabilities) is expected to fall 50-100 basis points over two years as the AAA rating filters through. With capital adequacy now near 33-34%, financial/solvency risk is low; the real risk here is business risk - how exposed used-vehicle and rural lending is to weak monsoons and agricultural stress, which is exactly what drove the recent guidance cut.
analysis.ownership_read: The promoter entity, Shriram Ownership Trust, now holds about 20.3%, down from 25.4% before the MUFG deal, and that remaining stake is locked in for three years with a right of first offer to MUFG. MUFG itself holds about 20% - a globally significant bank, not a passive financial investor, which is a notable and unusual anchor shareholder for an Indian NBFC. FIIs hold roughly 37-41% and DIIs roughly 18.7-19.9%. No pledging has been reported on promoter shares. No marquee Indian investor such as Piramal or a sovereign wealth fund currently appears on the register, as far as could be verified.
strengths: AUM crossed Rs 2.81 lakh crore, growing 15.7% year-on-year
Capital adequacy jumped to roughly 33-34% after MUFG's Rs 39,618 crore capital infusion, among the strongest buffers in Indian NBFCs
Credit rating upgraded to AAA by CRISIL, ICRA and India Ratings in 2026
Gross Stage 3 ratio improved to 4.57% from 5.32% a year earlier
watchpoints: FY27 AUM growth guidance cut to 15-17% from 18%, citing weak monsoon and drought in key lending states
Analysts (Jefferies) flagged credit costs could stay elevated for one to two more quarters; management itself guides to ~2% full-year credit cost
Return on equity diluted to roughly 12.76% after the MUFG equity issuance, below the historical mid-teens level
Stock down about 24% from its August 2026 peak; company had to publicly deny a report about MUFG possibly raising its stake above 50%
analysis.one_thing: Watch the Q3 results (expected around late January 2027) for whether AUM growth and credit costs stabilize in line with management's trimmed guidance, or whether the rural-demand weakness and elevated credit costs persist further.
analysis.data_notes: Cross-checked AUM, NIM, Stage 3 ratio and the MUFG deal terms across multiple sources (Business Standard, CRISIL/ICRA rating notes, Kotak/PL Capital, Whalesbook/Anand Rathi). PAT figures differ slightly between standalone (~Rs 2,307 crore) and consolidated (~Rs 2,314 crore) presentations and were not reconciled - verify on Screener or the company's exchange filing. ROCE and the exact next dividend record date could not be verified. Given how recent the reporting period is, some quarterly figures may lag the most current exchange filing - confirm against the latest results before publishing.
